optional_codes.reason: Lisinopril is a prescribed drug taken every day for a chronic condition, which fits category Z79, but no Tabular List instruction requires the code. Defensible either way.

unsupported_codes.reason: Hypertensive retinopathy: reporting a code from this subcategory states that the retinopathy is due to the hypertension. The provider lists the two as separate items and states no link.

citations.H35.00: ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY2027, Section I.A.19: the assignment of a diagnosis code is based on the provider's diagnostic statement that the condition exists. Section I.A.15: for conditions not specifically linked by relational terms in the classification, provider documentation must link the conditions in order to code them as related. The Alphabetic Index lists H35.00 beside the term 'Retinopathy (background)', with 'hypertensive' as a separate subterm, and has no entry for retinopathy under 'Hypertension, with'. Section IV.G: list first the code for the condition chiefly responsible for the services provided. Here the ophthalmologist's assessment lists retinopathy of both eyes and hypertension as two separate items and does not call the retinopathy hypertensive or link the two, so the retinopathy is reported with the code for unspecified background retinopathy; the visit is a follow-up of the retinopathy, so it is first-listed.
citations.I10: ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY2027, Section I.C.9.a.5: subcategory H35.0 should be used along with a code from categories I10 to I15 to include the systemic hypertension, and the sequencing is based on the reason for the encounter. Tabular List instruction at H35.0: code also any associated hypertension (I10). Section IV.J: code all documented conditions that coexist at the time of the visit and that require or affect patient care, treatment or management. Here hypertension is in the assessment, the blood pressure is high and the patient is sent to his primary care physician about it, so it is reported after the retinopathy.

coder_notes: The fundus findings and the history make hypertension the likely cause, but naming the cause is the provider's call. Reporting I10 beside H35.00 says that he has both conditions; it does not say that one caused the other. The narrowed arterioles, nicking, hemorrhages and cotton wool spots are the findings behind the diagnosis of retinopathy and are not coded beside it. He has no diabetes. The retinopathy was found a year ago and is still present, so neither a routine examination code nor a follow-up examination code applies. The blood pressure reading adds nothing beyond the hypertension code: he has an established diagnosis, and no hypertensive crisis is documented. In practice this documentation would lead to a provider query; the gold is what can be reported from the note as written.
